decision_reason: The closest unseen pair, sitting and lying on back, differs only in global posture inclination in A1. A torso-specific inclination adds an observable anatomical distinction without treating the seated load-bearing configuration as equivalent to trunk lean. Lateral torso inclination also distinguishes lying on back from its seen anchor lying on right side without relying on their unsupported smoothness difference. Retain the remaining concepts: the supplied capabilities do not justify reliable additional stair-direction, treadmill-slope, or elevator-specific attributes. Coverage diagnostics motivate these checks but do not establish predictability.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: torso_inclination
attributes.definition: Average departure of the torso's anatomical longitudinal direction from upright relative to gravity, irrespective of the inclination of the overall load-bearing body configuration.

levels.Medium: Torso is moderately inclined away from upright.
levels.High: Torso is strongly inclined or nearly horizontal.

attributes.name: torso_lateral_inclination
attributes.definition: Magnitude of the average gravity component along the torso's anatomical left-right direction, expressing sustained sideward rather than forward-backward torso inclination without distinguishing left from right.

levels.Low: Little sustained gravity component along the torso's left-right direction.
levels.Medium: Intermediate sustained gravity component along the torso's left-right direction.
levels.High: Gravity is predominantly aligned with the torso's left-right direction.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude. It provides broad transfer from walking and vigorous activities to stair locomotion and elevator movement. Effort, speed and individual execution make adjacent ordinal levels uncertain; no measured intensity differences are assumed.

cadence: G6 supports repeated leg and torso motion rates, transferring periodic locomotion from seen walking to stairs and flat treadmill walking. Slow repetition, short windows and irregular movement can obscure a meaningful cycle; cadence is not repetition count or regularity.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid acceleration changes, providing a transferable distinction between continuous treadmill motion and less smooth descent. Pace and execution introduce ambiguity. Static back-lying and side-lying need not differ in smoothness, so their A1 difference is not treated as a reliable posture cue.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: impulsiveness: G10 supports isolated rapid changes associated with contacts and landings, transferring impact semantics from jumping to descending stairs. Contact technique and attenuation at torso or leg sensors affect peak strength; elevator transitions cannot be presumed to occur in every window.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative segment orientations that inform the overall load-bearing configuration. Standing and side-lying anchor upright versus recumbent configurations for unseen static postures. Seated bodies are articulated rather than single rigid axes, making the intermediate global category less directly observable than torso inclination.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative body orientation. It transfers stable-versus-changing posture semantics from still elevator standing and rowing to elevator movement. Local limb cycling must not be mistaken for global posture change, and small steps may leave torso posture nearly constant.

rotational_motion: G2 supports sustained angular motion in torso and limbs, connecting seen walking to stairs and movement within an elevator. Limb swing can dominate without global turning; the label moving around does not guarantee a particular amount of rotation.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translation proxies, retaining progression semantics shared by outdoor walking and stair locomotion. Constant-velocity elevator travel and absolute displacement are not reliably observable from these capabilities; treadmill limb motion can also resemble overground motion. Preserve the concept without inventing direction or height-change attributes.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G11 supports recurrence and predictability, transferring structured treadmill motion versus less structured movement to flat treadmill walking and elevator movement. Brief or repetitive elevator movement may appear regular, and static signals can be predictable without having cadence.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: torso_inclination: G1 supports mean torso orientation relative to gravity. A typically upright seated torso contrasts with a horizontal back-lying torso, adding a second distinction to the closest unseen pair while standing and side-lying supply seen upright and horizontal anchors. This anatomical scope complements the global load-bearing attribute. Reclined sitting, trunk lean and anatomical sensor alignment create ambiguity; exact angles are not assumed.

torso_lateral_inclination: G1 supports the direction of gravity in the torso frame. Sustained lateral gravity distinguishes side-lying from back-lying even when both have horizontal torsos, replacing reliance on their incidental A1 smoothness difference. Seen side-lying supplies the lateral state and standing the nonlateral state. Interpretation requires consistent anatomical alignment; rolling, lateral lean and dynamic acceleration can blur intermediate states.

semantic_redundancy_review: The 11 attributes retain magnitude, repetition rate, sustained smoothness, isolated impacts, global posture, posture change, angular motion, translation and predictability as distinct concepts. Torso inclination partially overlaps global posture inclination but separates anatomical trunk attitude from an articulated load-bearing configuration, particularly for sitting. Torso lateral inclination describes the direction of tilt rather than its total magnitude, distinguishing back-lying from side-lying. Cadence is distinct from regularity, and smoothness from impulsiveness. No additional stair-direction, elevation, equipment-identity or arm-participation attribute is introduced because its stable discriminability is not established by the supplied semantics and capabilities.
